headings.title: Cooking-facility certification, investigation, and permit issuance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires permit applicants to certify garbage-cooking facilities and directs prompt investigation and permit issuance by the director of agriculture or deputy if facilities are adequate.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 266.440:14414, both subsections, and history note (L. 1953 p. 6 §§ 3, 4), and verified all fingerprints. Confirmed clear distinction between subsection 1 (selling or transporting unlawfully garbage-fed swine) and subsection 2 (knowingly purchasing unlawfully garbage-fed swine); retained both titles.

headings.title: Prohibition on selling or transporting unlawfully garbage-fed swine
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1953 p. 6 §§ 3, 4). Distinguished from subsection 2 by prohibiting selling or transporting swine fed garbage in violation of sections 266.410 to 266.460, without subsection 2's knowledge element.

headings.title: Prohibition on knowingly purchasing unlawfully garbage-fed swine
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 1 by prohibiting knowingly purchasing swine fed garbage in violation of sections 266.410 to 266.460.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 266.520:14421, both subsections, and notes (L. 1976 H.B. 1630 § 5, A.L. 1985 S.B. 65; Effective 5-30-85), and verified all fingerprints. Confirmed "director" means the Missouri agricultural experiment station director per section 266.505(6) (clarified in subsection 1 reviewNote), checked semiannual reporting, fee caps/defaults, invoice disclosure, and authorized experiment/education uses; retained both titles.

headings.title: Semiannual sales certificates and tonnage inspection fees
headings.reviewNote: Independently reviewed complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1976 H.B. 1630 § 5, A.L. 1985 S.B. 65; Effective 5-30-85). Requires producers and distributors to file semiannual sales certificates with the director (director of the Missouri agricultural experiment station per section 266.505(6)) within thirty days after June thirtieth and December thirty-first and pay a rule-prescribed fee capped at ten cents per ton or eleven cents per metric ton (or a four-cent/4.4-cent default if no fee is prescribed).

headings.title: Invoice disclosure and authorized uses of inspection fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires stating the inspection fee on sales statements or invoices and authorizes using fees for administration under sections 266.500 to 266.550, Missouri agricultural experiment station experiments, related research, publications, and farmer education.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 266.530:14423, all six subsections, and history note (L. 1976 H.B. 1630 § 7), and verified all fingerprints. Confirmed "director" means the Missouri agricultural experiment station director per section 266.505(6) (clarified in subsection 4 reviewNote), verified fixed-plant versus portable-plant sampling, rolling three-sample average, truck-sample exclusion, producer notice, and sieve methods; retained all six titles.

headings.title: Production belt, stockpile, and fixed-plant sampling requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1976 H.B. 1630 § 7). Covers obtaining samples from production belts or uncertified stockpiles, minimum eight annual samples at permanent fixed plants, and the limit of one official sample per day per stockpile or belt.

headings.title: Sampling requirements for portable plants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 1 by governing monthly sampling where no permanent fixed plant exists while a portable plant is on site until at least eight annual samples accumulate.

headings.title: Rolling three-sample average for guaranteed analysis
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Establishes the initial three-sample average for guaranteed analysis and ongoing recalculation by dropping the oldest sample and adding the newest.

headings.title: Authorized samplers and exclusion of truck samples from averages
headings.reviewNote: Independently reviewed complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Distinguishes production-belt sampling (by producer/distributor in the presence of an appointee of the director, i.e., the Missouri agricultural experiment station director per section 266.505(6)) from stockpile sampling (only by director-appointed persons with prior notice), and excludes truck or other-point samples from source guaranteed-analysis averages.

headings.title: Producer and distributor notice for sampling
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires producers and distributors to notify the director or authorized persons of production or distribution so compliance samples may be taken.

headings.title: Compliance with regulatory official sieve analysis methods
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Requires all samples for analysis to follow official sieve analysis methods set forth in regulations.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 266.540:14425, all five subsections, and history note (L. 1976 H.B. 1630 § 9), and verified all fingerprints. Confirmed "director" means the Missouri agricultural experiment station director per section 266.505(6) (clarified in subsection 1 reviewNote), checked mailed section 266.535 certifications, segregated stockpiles, pre-enactment stockpiles, delivering party guarantee responsibility, and adjusting nonconforming material analyses; retained all five titles.

headings.title: Written certification of section 266.535 analysis results
headings.reviewNote: Independently reviewed complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1976 H.B. 1630 § 9). Requires the director (director of the Missouri agricultural experiment station per section 266.505(6)) to certify calcium carbonate equivalent, magnesium content, fineness, and effective magnesium and neutralizing material per ton by U.S. mail upon receiving section 266.535 analyses.

headings.title: Separate certification for segregated and sampled stockpiles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Permits separate certifications for stockpiles that are kept separated from other stockpiles and sampled under sections 266.500 to 266.550.

headings.title: Coverage of liming materials stockpiled before enactment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Subjects agricultural liming materials produced and stockpiled prior to enactment of sections 266.500 to 266.550 to the same sampling and certification provisions.

headings.title: Delivering producer or distributor responsibility for guarantees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Vests final responsibility for effective magnesium and neutralizing material guarantees in the producer or distributor making delivery for soil application.

headings.title: Adjusting guaranteed analysis before selling nonconforming material
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Permits a producer or distributor holding liming material that fails to meet its guaranteed analysis to sell it only after adjusting the guaranteed analysis to the correct analyses.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 266.543:14426, all six subsections including subdivisions 2(1)–(5) and 3(1)–(3), and notes (L. 1985 S.B. 65; Effective 5-30-85), and verified all fingerprints. Confirmed "director" means the Missouri agricultural experiment station director per section 266.505(6) (clarified in subsection 1 reviewNote) and verified subsection 5 faithfully preserves the archived statutory cross-reference to fertilizer-law fees under sections 266.291 to 266.351 without inventing a correction; retained all six titles.

headings.title: Advisory council composition and appointment
headings.reviewNote: Independently reviewed complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1985 S.B. 65; Effective 5-30-85). Covers appointment by the director (director of the Missouri agricultural experiment station per section 266.505(6)) of the nine-member advisory council consisting of three limestone producers, three farmers, and three at-large residents selected with majority approval of the other six members.

headings.title: Advisory council duties, rule approval, and fee advice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, including subdivisions (1) through (5), plus notes. Covers annual meetings, income and expenditure review, reviewing and approving all director rules and revisions/rescissions, advising on fees in the best interests of Missouri farmers, and general advisory duties under sections 266.500 to 266.550.

headings.title: Three-year terms and staggered initial appointments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, including subdivisions (1) through (3), plus notes. Sets three-year terms until successors qualify, with staggered initial one-, two-, and three-year terms.

headings.title: Residency requirement, term limits, and reappointment waiting period
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Requires Missouri residency, bars serving more than two consecutive terms, and permits reappointment after at least three years off the council.

headings.title: Expense reimbursement from sections 266.291 to 266.351 fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Provides for reasonable expense reimbursement under the director's policy and preserves the archived statutory cross-reference requiring payment from fees collected under sections 266.291 to 266.351 (fertilizer law fees).

headings.title: Filling advisory council vacancies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and notes. Covers vacancy appointments by the director with majority approval of remaining members, matching predecessor qualifications, for the unexpired term.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 266.545:14427, all three subsections including subdivisions 2(1)–(7), and history note (through A.L. 1995 S.B. 3), and verified all fingerprints. Confirmed "director" means the Missouri agricultural experiment station director per section 266.505(6) (clarified in subsection 1 reviewNote), verified majority advisory council rule-approval prerequisite, enforcement/audit/stop-sale/permit powers, and section 536.024 compliance; retained all three titles.

headings.title: Enforcement duty, rulemaking, and advisory council approval
headings.reviewNote: Independently reviewed complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1976 H.B. 1630 § 10, A.L. 1985 S.B. 65, A.L. 1993 S.B. 52, A.L. 1995 S.B. 3). Vests enforcement and administration of sections 266.500 to 266.550 in the director (director of the Missouri agricultural experiment station per section 266.505(6)) and requires chapter 536 rules, revisions, or rescissions to receive majority advisory council approval before filing with the secretary of state.

headings.title: Sampling, audit, stop-sale, reporting, and permit powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, including subdivisions (1) through (7), plus history note. Covers sampling/analysis, business-hours entry, sales record audits, stop-sale/use/removal orders, laboratory and staffing, annual public reports with statewide composite financial and tonnage statements, and permit revocation, suspension, or refusal for willful violations or unpaid fees.

headings.title: Rulemaking compliance with section 536.024
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Conditions effectiveness of rules under sections 266.500 to 266.550 on promulgation pursuant to section 536.024.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 266.550:14428, both subsections, and history note (L. 1976 H.B. 1630 § 11), and verified all fingerprints. Verified effective neutralizing material and effective magnesium per-ton guarantees and required disclosures on bills of lading, scale tickets, delivery receipts, and other instruments of sale; retained both titles.

headings.title: Required neutralizing material and magnesium guarantees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1976 H.B. 1630 § 11). Requires all agricultural liming materials sold, offered, or exposed for sale to guarantee effective neutralizing material and effective magnesium per ton.

headings.title: Required disclosures on shipping and sale instruments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires sellers, shippers, transporters, and deliverers to affix net weight, effective magnesium and neutralizing material guarantees, brand name if any, and manufacturer/producer/shipper name and principal office to every bill of lading, scale ticket, delivery receipt, or other instrument of sale.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 266.600:35135, both subsections, and history note (L. 2018 S.B. 627 & 925), and verified all fingerprints. Verified local regulation preemption for seeds/fertilizers under sections 266.021 and 266.291, pre-August 28, 2018 grandfather exception, and rice seed exclusion; retained both titles.

headings.title: Local regulation preemption and pre-August 28, 2018 exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2018 S.B. 627 & 925). Prohibits political subdivisions from adopting or enforcing ordinances, rules, or regulations on labeling, cultivation, or other use of seeds or fertilizers as defined or used in sections 266.021 and 266.291, while exempting enactments adopted prior to August 28, 2018.

headings.title: Exclusion of rice seed
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Excludes rice seed from the applicability of section 266.600.
